subject: Coord: Renewal + add'l apps (Analytics & Insights) — draft SOW and per-key quotas
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@delta-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Expansion + renewal: proposal for additional apps and updated term

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposal so we can align with procurement:

Summary of ask
- Delta wants to add two new projects under the same tenant: "Analytics Dashboard" (internal BI) and "Customer Insights" (product-facing).
- Approx. 8 additional service API keys (one per microservice/team) + scoped quotas per key.
- Increase committed throughput by ~35% to cover peak inference for both projects.
- Targeting a renewal/extension to align on a 12-month term from Jan 1, 2027.

What we propose (draft)
- 12-month renewal with an amended SOW (attached: Delta_SOW_v3.pdf).
- Per-key quotas (can be set per-project) + ability to burst to shared pool (50k tokens/team for first 60 days).
- Pricing: base renewal rate as discussed on the call; we will model a 6-month ramp with optional volume discount (details in attached pricing sheet).

Next steps I suggest
1) I'll share the revised SOW & pricing (attached).
2) Prod/SE (cc'd) will propose the per-key quota map we recommend based on your current traffic shape.
3) If procurement is happy, we route to DocuSign for a signature; earliest effective date requested: 2027-01-01.

Attachments: Delta_SOW_v3.pdf, Delta_Pricing_2026Q4.xlsx

If this looks good, can you confirm who from procurement should receive the SOW?

Best,

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@delta-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@delta-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Expansion + renewal: proposal for additional apps and updated term

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifying Qs before we loop in procurement: 

1) Per-route quotas: can we carve strict per-key token caps (hard limits) rather than soft allocations? Some of our teams run unattended jobs and we need enforcement.
2) Burst pool: is that applied automatically or requires opt-in per key? Is there throttling if the shared pool is exhausted?
3) SLA: any change to latency SLOs for the expanded capacity? We have a few endpoints that require 99th percentile <200ms.

Also, procurement will likely want to see a redlined SOW and the invoice cadence (Net 45 or Net 60). Who should I send that to?

Evan
Director of Platform Engineering
Delta Analytics
ev an.cole@delta-analytics.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@delta-analytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Expansion + renewal: proposal for additional apps and updated term

Hi Evan —

Thanks — answers below inline and a proposed configuration.

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 11:02 AM Evan Cole <evan.cole@delta-analytics.com> wrote:
> 1) Per-route quotas: can we carve strict per-key token caps (hard limits) rather than soft allocations? Some of our teams run unattended jobs and we need enforcement.

Yes — we support hard caps per API key. We'll enforce quota at the routing layer; requests exceeding the cap will receive 429 with a clear X-RateLimit header. We'll include per-key alerts for 80%/95% thresholds.

> 2) Burst pool: is that applied automatically or requires opt-in per key? Is there throttling if the shared pool is exhausted?

Burst pool is opt-in per key. For the initial 60-day trial we can enable automatic burst, but you can toggle it per-key in Console. If the shared pool is exhausted, traffic falls back to the base committed rate; we won't silently throttle below guaranteed SLOs — instead requests will be queued or receive 429 depending on latency window.

> 3) SLA: any change to latency SLOs for the expanded capacity? We have a few endpoints that require 99th percentile <200ms.

Our Dedicated tier SLA remains the same. For endpoints requiring <200ms at 99th, we'll map those routes to a high-priority pod group and reserve capacity — SE (Aditya) will propose exact pod sizing. If you need contractual SLOs for those routes, we can add a route-level SLA appendix to the SOW.

Proposed per-key mapping (draft)
- Analytics Dashboard: 3 keys, 40k tokens/day each, reserved medium-priority pod group.
- Customer Insights: 3 keys, 60k tokens/day each, reserved high-priority pod group for latency-sensitive routes.
- Shared integrations & infra: 2 keys for background batch jobs, 120k tokens/day combined, burst opt-in.

I'll get the SE sizing and a redline-ready SOW over to you by tomorrow. For procurement, please cc procure@delta-analytics.com and Priya (copied). Our billing team supports Net 45 as standard; we can do Net 60 with exec approval — I'll flag that.

Attachments referenced: Delta_SOW_v3.pdf (updated with per-route appendix), Delta_Pricing_2026Q4.xlsx

Best,
—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Expansion + renewal: proposal for additional apps and updated term

Looping in a pricing tweak suggestion — this is internal.

Thanks for drafting, Soojin. Delta looks like a strong expansion opportunity; to grease the deal I propose the following commercial sweetener:
- 15% volume discount on generated tokens for the first 6 months post-effective date (applies to the additional committed capacity only).
- Maintain current per-token list price for existing commit baseline.

Please confirm if SE (Aditya) is comfortable with reserved pod sizing and if the 60-day burst is safe from an ops perspective. Also want an updated ARR impact piece for Rev Ops before we send to procurement.

Thanks,
—
Lauren Bishop
VP, Growth — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Expansion + renewal: proposal for additional apps and updated term

Quick SE notes on the proposed mapping — technical feasibility looks good. A few implementation details: 
- Per-key hard caps: implemented at edge routing; recommend soft-fail early (80% alert) + hard cap enforcement.
- Pod sizing: for Customer Insights (latency sensitive) we should use 2 x A100 equivalent reservation for 99p <200ms at expected peak QPS. Will validate with live traffic samples.
- Prefix/KV caching: for Analytics Dashboard, enable prefix caching for common prompts to reduce cost by ~18% in our estimate (details in pricing sheet).
- Tokenization nuance: background jobs may have longer sequences — ensure KV cache TTL and max seq length are set per key to avoid cache thrash.

I'm comfortable with the 60-day burst as long as alerting and automatic throttling are configured; ops should be able to opt-out per-key if needed.

—
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
